PurchasedTraits.Name: Purchased Traits
PurchasedTraits.Description: You have 3 ancestry points to spend on the following traits. (Quick Build: Glowing Recovery, Grounded.)

Relentless.Name: Relentless
Relentless.Description: Whenever a creature deals damage to you that leaves you dying, you can make a free strike against any creature. If that creature is reduced to 0 Stamina by your strike, you can spend a Recovery.

BloodfireRush.Name: Bloodfire Rush
BloodfireRush.Description:
The engineered fire in your veins makes you run faster in the heat of battle. The first time in any combat round that you take damage, you gain a +2 bonus to speed until the end of the round.

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.gGW48sXk6lvWf9ZW.ActiveEffect.NVGTtYA1twMvPbnS]
BloodfireRush.EffectDescription: The engineered fire in your veins makes you run faster in the heat of battle. The first time in any combat round that you take damage, you gain a +2 bonus to speed until the end of the round.

GlowingRecovery.Name: Glowing Recovery
GlowingRecovery.Description: Your bloodfire allows you to regain your strength quicker than others. Whenever you use the Catch Breath maneuver, you can spend as many Recoveries as you like.

Grounded.Name: Grounded
Grounded.Description: The density of your frame makes it difficult for others to move you. You have a +1 bonus to stability.

Nonstop.Name: Nonstop
Nonstop.Description: Your bloodfire supplies you with a constant rush of adrenaline. You can’t be made slowed.

PassionateArtisan.Name: Passionate Artisan
PassionateArtisan.Description: When you are stirred by a passion for creation, your bloodfire lets you work longer and harder. When you gain your initial skills from your career, culture, class, or other source, choose two skills from the crafting skill group, whether you have those skills or not. Whenever you make a project roll for a crafting project that uses these skills, you gain a +2 bonus to the roll.

Changer.Name: Changer
Changer.Description:
A were-blooded shapeshifter who walks as a human, fights as a hybrid war-beast, and runs as a true animal.

Lineage (required)

Pick one lineage at creation. It is always on and stays on your sheet as a feature: @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.liCuEIuHFCtAZwzi]{Raven} (Walk + Fly), @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.L5Fj6nVEju6s361I]{Rat} (size 1S), or @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.7KRwCZ8xwI2nuOhI]{Wolf} (+2 speed).

Forms

Every Changer gains @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.qhrDc59fcOPiaNMh]{Changer Forms}: Human, Hybrid (War), and Beast. Changing form is a maneuver, and exactly one form is active at a time. You start in Human Form.

Changer Traits

Changer heroes have access to the following traits.

Signature Trait: @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.GvoBzKeb871MArtN]{Beast-Hide}

Purchased Changer Traits

You have 3 ancestry points to spend on the following traits. (Quick Build: Savage Burst, Layered Hide.)

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.yw3LAnJVKy0R4PS1]{Pack Guard (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.AnY2ro2slwfNEZSc]{Feral Cry (2 Points)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.SZT2y1ndFs2vR5IG]{Savage Burst (2 Points)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.fvEbDEwHmBGxLc4A]{Layered Hide (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.IeVv5koMNTrHIJn8]{Beast’s Resolve (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.2c4zUgqqgULDY4WR]{Beast Movement (2 Points)}

PurchasedTraits.Name: Purchased Traits
PurchasedTraits.Description: You have 3 ancestry points to spend on the following traits. (Quick Build: Savage Burst, Layered Hide.)

Lineage.Name: Lineage (required)
Lineage.Description: Choose exactly one lineage: Raven, Rat, or Wolf. Your lineage is always on. Don’t confirm character creation without choosing one.

BeastHide.Name: Beast-Hide
BeastHide.Description: Your hardened hide, fur, or feathers grant you damage immunity equal to [[lookup @level]]{your level} to one of the following damage types: acid, cold, corruption, fire, lightning, or poison. You can change your immunity type when you finish a respite.

PackGuard.Name: Pack Guard
PackGuard.Description: Whenever you or an adjacent creature takes damage from a strike, you can use a triggered action to guard against the blow. You reduce any damage from the strike by an [[/heal @level]]{amount equal to your level}.

FeralCry.Name: Feral Cry
FeralCry.Story: You let loose a piercing shriek, chittering screech, or bone-deep howl to shake your foes’ spirits.

SavageBurst.Name: Savage Burst
SavageBurst.Story: A battering downdraft, a filthy venomous lunge, or a rending pounce tears into your foes.
SavageBurst.Effect: You choose the ability’s damage type from acid, cold, corruption, fire, lightning, or poison.

LayeredHide.Name: Layered Hide
LayeredHide.Description: Select one damage immunity granted by your Beast-Hide trait. You always have this immunity, in addition to the immunity granted by Beast-Hide.

BeastsResolve.Name: Beast’s Resolve
BeastsResolve.Description: As a maneuver, you can recite your resolve. Until the start of your next turn, whenever you make a saving throw, you succeed on a 4 or higher.
BeastsResolve.EffectDescription: Until the start of your next turn, whenever you make a saving throw, you succeed on a 4 or higher.

BeastMovement.Name: Beast Movement
BeastMovement.Description: You can move as your lineage flies or bounds. Raven: true flight. Rat/Wolf: prodigious leaping and climbing bounds. Either way, you can stay aloft for a number of rounds equal to [[lookup formula="max(@M, 1)" evaluate=true]]{your Physique score (minimum 1 round)} before you come down. While moving this way at 3rd level or lower, you have damage weakness 5.
BeastMovement.Director: Two active effects are included in this trait: one for heroes in echelon 1, another for echelon 2+. Players should keep the one that applies.
BeastMovement.Echelon1Description: While moving this way, you can stay aloft for a number of rounds equal to [[lookup @M]]{your Physique score} (minimum 1 round) before you come down. At 3rd level or lower, you have damage weakness 5 while doing so.
BeastMovement.Echelon2Description: While moving this way, you can stay aloft for a number of rounds equal to [[lookup @M]]{your Physique score} (minimum 1 round) before you come down.

Raven.Name: Raven Lineage
Raven.Description:
Cunning, aerial, uncanny. Your movement types are Walk and Fly.

Your Beast-Hide reads as oily black feathers with an iridescent sheen. Your Feral Cry is a piercing shriek and your Savage Burst a battering downdraft of wings and beak. In Beast Form you are a raven.
Raven.EffectDescription: Your movement types are Walk and Fly.

Rat.Name: Rat Lineage
Rat.Description:
Fast, resilient, swarming. Your size is 1S.

Your Beast-Hide reads as matted grey fur, scarred and tough. Your Feral Cry is a chittering screech and your Savage Burst a filthy, venomous lunge. In Beast Form you are a rat.

Wolf.Name: Wolf Lineage
Wolf.Description:
Ferocious, pack-minded, direct. You gain a +2 bonus to speed.

Your Beast-Hide reads as a thick pelt with bristling hackles. Your Feral Cry is a bone-deep howl and your Savage Burst a rending pounce. In Beast Form you are a wolf.

Forms.Name: Changer Forms
Forms.Description:
You have three forms. Changing form is a maneuver. Exactly one form is active at a time, and you start in Human Form.

Human Form: You gain an edge on tests to pass as or blend in among baseline humans. You show no obvious beast tells.

Hybrid (War) Form: You gain an edge on Intimidation tests, and your melee free strikes deal +1 damage. You are visibly a war-beast and can’t pass as human.

Beast Form: You gain an edge on Stealth and Perception tests. You can’t use manufactured weapons, and you can’t speak clear language (growls and body language only).

In Foundry: enable the matching form effect on the Effects tab when you change form; enabling one form turns the others off.

Human.Name: Form: Human
Human.Description: You gain an edge on tests to pass as or blend in among baseline humans (not automated — apply the edge when the test calls for it). You show no obvious beast tells.

Hybrid.Name: Form: Hybrid
Hybrid.Description: You gain an edge on Intimidation tests (automated). Your melee free strikes deal +1 damage (not automated — add it to the roll). You are visibly a war-beast and can’t pass as human.

Beast.Name: Form: Beast
Beast.Description: You gain an edge on Stealth and Perception tests (automated). You can’t use manufactured weapons, and you can’t speak clear language (growls and body language only).

Warnings.MissingLineage: {name} is a Changer without a Lineage. Open the Changer ancestry, find the Lineage advancement, and reconfigure it to choose Raven, Rat, or Wolf.

Mutant.Name: Mutant
Mutant.Description:
Powerful, unstable, endlessly customizable — human clay reshaped by the Dark One’s touch.

Humans whose flesh has been rewritten — inherited taint, corrupted-zone exposure, magical accident, infernal bargain, or corp gene-forging. Born or made carries no mechanical difference. They are the People most directly marked by the cosmic war: living proof the Dark One’s touch can remake baseline humanity into something else.

Mutant Traits

Signature Trait: @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.dzbVd5iIaHGBULBC]{Aberrant Rapport}

Purchased Mutant Traits

You have 3 ancestry points to spend on the following traits. (Quick Build: Warped Legs, Ossified Crown.)

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.oSFPoMJn8orsYLUY]{Barbed Mutation (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.ukswcD6uWCcwIg62]{Warped Legs (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.LM0o1d9TaqZDjhU4]{Taint Flare (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.CQ1T0rjR6SbKe4VO]{Taint Sight (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.7xCzjYKMltkS2PiM]{Ossified Crown (2 Points)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.9MFaJjqNH5uGtN2s]{Prehensile Mutation (2 Points)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.a5qD9riHweABLtJO]{Membrane Wings (2 Points)}

Corruptive Flaw (optional)

At creation you can pick a cosmetic Corruptive Flaw, such as Visible Taint, Hungering Cells, Unstable Form, Taint Sink, or Fractured Mind. It costs no ancestry points and has no mechanical effect: it is color for tells, roleplay, and scenes. There is no Corruption Load meter.

PurchasedTraits.Name: Purchased Traits
PurchasedTraits.Description: You have 3 ancestry points to spend on the following traits. (Quick Build: Warped Legs, Ossified Crown.)

AberrantRapport.Name: Aberrant Rapport
AberrantRapport.Description: Your taint twists how your words and presence are read, giving you a better read on people and a way to steer them. You have one skill of your choice from the social skill group, and you gain an edge on tests when attempting to discover an NPC’s motivations and pitfalls during a negotiation.

BarbedMutation.Name: Barbed Mutation
BarbedMutation.Description: A barbed spur, spine, or tendril punctuates your strikes. Once per round when you make a melee strike, you can deal extra damage with the strike equal to [[/damage max(@M,@A,@R,@I,@P)]]{your highest characteristic score}.

WarpedLegs.Name: Warped Legs
WarpedLegs.Description: Your mutated legs make you faster. You have speed 6.
WarpedLegs.EffectDescription: Your mutated legs make you faster. You have speed 6.

TaintFlare.Name: Taint Flare
TaintFlare.Description:
When your taint flares under stress, it lashes back. Whenever you take damage from a creature, you can use a triggered action to deal that creature psychic damage equal to [[/damage 1d10+@level type=psychic]]{1d10 + your level}.

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.91UYvxXgCyETqxIh]{Taint Flare}

TaintFlareAbility.Name: Taint Flare
TaintFlareAbility.Story: Your taint flares under stress and lashes back.
TaintFlareAbility.Effect: You deal [[/damage 1d10+@level type=psychic]]{1d10 + your level psychic damage} to that creature.

TaintSight.Name: Taint Sight
TaintSight.Description: Mutated eyes see through darkness, fog, and other obscuring effects. You don’t take a bane on strikes made against creatures with concealment.

OssifiedCrown.Name: Ossified Crown
OssifiedCrown.Description: Bone plates, horn-like growths, or a hardened cranial ridge mark your force of will. Whenever you make a saving throw, you succeed on a roll of 5 or higher.
OssifiedCrown.EffectDescription: Whenever you make a saving throw, you succeed on a roll of 5 or higher.

PrehensileMutation.Name: Prehensile Mutation
PrehensileMutation.Description: A prehensile tendril, extra limb, or living appendage lets you challenge foes on all sides. You can’t be flanked.

MembraneWings.Name: Membrane Wings
MembraneWings.Description:
Patagia, bone-and-skin wings, or similar membranes are strong enough to take you airborne. While using them to fly, you can stay aloft for a number of rounds equal to [[lookup formula="max(@M, 1)" evaluate=true]]{your Physique score (minimum 1 round)} before you fall. While flying at 3rd level or lower, you have damage weakness 5.

Enable a Membrane Wings effect on your sheet while you fly: echelon 1 (fly and damage weakness 5) at 3rd level or lower, or echelon 2+ (fly only) from 4th level.
MembraneWings.Echelon1Description: You fly. While flying at 3rd level or lower, you have damage weakness 5. You can stay aloft for a number of rounds equal to your Physique score (minimum 1 round) before you fall.
MembraneWings.Echelon2Description: You fly. You can stay aloft for a number of rounds equal to your Physique score (minimum 1 round) before you fall.

Cyborg.Name: Cyborg
Cyborg.Description:
Machine-first threshold beings — integrated, augmented, existentially unstable. Distinct from chrome-augmented meat.

A Cyborg is the far end of the chrome spectrum: effectively all organic Body Integrity spent, frame and cortex first. Living, non-Cyborg heroes who want implants use the Chrome chapter; the Cyborg does not. Full conversion is made, not bred — surgery, battlefield salvage, corp programs, or voluntary upload into a shell.

Cyborg Traits

Signature Trait: @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.GKKVzsE7uO4HLYDi]{Cortical Firewall}

Hard constraints: @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.dgBmVGmpoJ8cqmVO]{Arcane Severance}

Purchased Cyborg Traits

You have 3 ancestry points to spend on the following traits. (Quick Build: Penetration Optics, Installed Suite with Particle Lance.)

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.wEQTCGWeWxbrD3Y3]{Penetration Optics (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.1AEnOK1gTEHjOLEj]{Predictive Sensors (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.hFbUGmW7WZXkc7kp]{Auxiliary Limbs — Athletics (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.bEJrcH33ekVQ92H6]{Auxiliary Limbs — Combat (2 Points)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.pVsfJpZi2gkskLqr]{Installed Suite (2 Points)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.zLXYWyfkOXSA7IEx]{Locked Processors (2 Points)}

Hard Constraints

Arcane Severance: You can’t use Magic-keyword abilities. You are barred from the Elementalist and Street Priest classes, and from any Veil-casting path that requires Magic. The Tech-keyword Installed Suite abilities from this ancestry are allowed. You can still be targeted, harmed, or protected by magic.

Tech-only recovery: You are healed by tech, Wrench-style repair, or Medic tech procedures as your table defines, not by Magic healing (Director’s call on Troubadour-style and similar effects).

System Crisis: When you would die under the usual 0 Stamina and dying rules, you instead enter a Director-facing System Crisis (machine failure) rather than a normal organic death spiral. This is a rule pointer only; the full Crisis table isn’t defined yet.

These are Ghostwire chargen and setting rules. They cost no ancestry points. Cyborgs don’t use the Chrome / Body Integrity chapter.

PurchasedTraits.Name: Purchased Traits
PurchasedTraits.Description: You have 3 ancestry points to spend on the following traits. (Quick Build: Penetration Optics, Installed Suite with Particle Lance.)

CorticalFirewall.Name: Cortical Firewall
CorticalFirewall.Description: Hardened cortex shielding and trauma-scarred processors blunt psychic assault. You have psychic immunity equal to [[lookup @level]]{your level}.

ArcaneSeverance.Name: Arcane Severance
ArcaneSeverance.Description:
Arcane Severance: You can’t use Magic-keyword abilities. You are barred from the Elementalist and Street Priest classes, and from any Veil-casting path that requires Magic. The Tech-keyword Installed Suite abilities from this ancestry are allowed. You can still be targeted, harmed, or protected by magic.

Tech-only recovery: You are healed by tech, Wrench-style repair, or Medic tech procedures as your table defines, not by Magic healing (Director’s call on Troubadour-style and similar effects).

System Crisis: When you would die under the usual 0 Stamina and dying rules, you instead enter a Director-facing System Crisis (machine failure) rather than a normal organic death spiral. This is a rule pointer only; the full Crisis table isn’t defined yet.

These are Ghostwire chargen and setting rules. They cost no ancestry points. Cyborgs don’t use the Chrome / Body Integrity chapter.

PenetrationOptics.Name: Penetration Optics
PenetrationOptics.Description:
As a maneuver, you adjust your vision to see through mundane obstructions up to 1 square thick. While your vision is adjusted this way, you can’t see and have no line of effect to creatures or objects within 1 square of you. You can restore your normal vision as a maneuver.

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.gk78dbMJirlXnW6y]{Penetration Optics}

PenetrationOpticsAbility.Name: Penetration Optics
PenetrationOpticsAbility.Effect: You adjust your vision to see through mundane obstructions up to 1 square thick. While your vision is adjusted this way, you can’t see and have no line of effect to creatures or objects within 1 square of you. You can restore your normal vision as a maneuver.

PredictiveSensors.Name: Predictive Sensors
PredictiveSensors.Description: Your sensors automatically know the location of concealed (not hidden) creatures within 20 squares, and you negate the bane on strikes against them. When you are targeted by a strike, you can use a triggered action to impose a bane on the power roll.

AuxiliaryLimbsAthletics.Name: Auxiliary Limbs — Athletics
AuxiliaryLimbsAthletics.Description: You gain an edge on Athletics and Acrobatics tests when you can use all your limbs.

AuxiliaryLimbsCombat.Name: Auxiliary Limbs — Combat
AuxiliaryLimbsCombat.Description: When you use Grab or Knockback against an adjacent creature, you can target one additional adjacent creature, using the same power roll for both. You can have up to two creatures grabbed at once.

InstalledSuite.Name: Installed Suite
InstalledSuite.Description:
Choose one piece of installed hardware. It grants one of the following signature abilities, usable at will. These are Tech abilities — chrome weapon mounts, particle projectors, and servo overrides — not psionic or magic powers.

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.Peqr7g7HZOH2OscM]{Kinetic Driver}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.HVyHEUARAnj2D0f6]{Particle Lance}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.HYHaUsaTfTMvV8ws]{Servo Overclock}

KineticDriver.Name: Kinetic Driver
KineticDriver.Story: A mag-rail driver in your frame fires a focused kinetic slug that hammers the target.

ParticleLance.Name: Particle Lance
ParticleLance.Story: A coherent particle lance fires from a projector built into your frame.

ServoOverclock.Name: Servo Overclock
ServoOverclock.Story: You dump power into servos — your own, or an ally’s gear through a wireless override.
ServoOverclock.Effect: The target gains a bonus to speed equal to [[lookup formula="max(@R, @I, @P)" evaluate=true]]{your Logic, Instinct, or Persona score (your choice)} until the start of your next turn.

LockedProcessors.Name: Locked Processors
LockedProcessors.Description: Hardened process priority keeps your mind online. You can’t be made dazed.

Revenant.Name: Revenant
Revenant.Description:
The dead who refused to stay down — driven by unfinished vengeance.

No one is born a Revenant. A person who died with a burning purpose rises again, sustained by will, keeping memories and personality.

Revenant Traits

Signature Trait: @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.JD7nJvUCKOHMCTWo]{Tough But Withered}

Former Life (choose one People you were before you died):

  • @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.E50vuGbpRAR1tEiG]{Former Life: Pure Human}
  • @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.kcq8w02zX4pf8qxl]{Former Life: Corran}
  • @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.FOXPE9fot3N9Jxs4]{Former Life: Elvani}
  • @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.nCpyldyrfOVS3OG9]{Former Life: Goliar}
  • @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.X4ai6DF083LzFtjc]{Former Life: Changer}
  • @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.GDoxeZM9K62j9dgl]{Former Life: Mutant}
  • @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.UYu7KmyAIL1xVGe7]{Former Life: Cyborg}

Purchased Revenant Traits

You have 2 ancestry points to spend on the following traits, or 3 ancestry points if your size is 1S (use the Revenant (Small) ancestry). (Quick Build: Bloodless, plus Undead Influence if size 1S.)

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.GpVnUPocyfBDlOLU]{Bloodless (2 Points)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.1e7sbAXjl4JFHKWl]{Previous Life: 1 Point (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.EFsFl4QlFNKWhojE]{Previous Life: 2 Points (2 Points)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.zSrXEtjbsdDzbPEY]{Undead Influence (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.1CCRqQC3LzYkpAhs]{Vengeance Mark (2 Points)}

PurchasedTraits.Name: Purchased Traits
PurchasedTraits.Description: You have 2 ancestry points to spend on the following traits. (Quick Build: Bloodless.)

Small.Name: Revenant (Small)
Small.Description:
Use this version of the Revenant if your Former Life size is 1S (such as a Rat-lineage Changer). It sets your size to 1S and gives you 3 ancestry points instead of 2.

Revenant Traits

Signature Trait: @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.JD7nJvUCKOHMCTWo]{Tough But Withered}

Former Life (choose one People you were before you died):

  • @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.E50vuGbpRAR1tEiG]{Former Life: Pure Human}
  • @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.kcq8w02zX4pf8qxl]{Former Life: Corran}
  • @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.FOXPE9fot3N9Jxs4]{Former Life: Elvani}
  • @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.nCpyldyrfOVS3OG9]{Former Life: Goliar}
  • @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.X4ai6DF083LzFtjc]{Former Life: Changer}
  • @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.GDoxeZM9K62j9dgl]{Former Life: Mutant}
  • @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.UYu7KmyAIL1xVGe7]{Former Life: Cyborg}

Purchased Revenant Traits

You have 3 ancestry points to spend on the following traits. (Quick Build: Bloodless, Undead Influence.)

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.GpVnUPocyfBDlOLU]{Bloodless (2 Points)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.1e7sbAXjl4JFHKWl]{Previous Life: 1 Point (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.EFsFl4QlFNKWhojE]{Previous Life: 2 Points (2 Points)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.zSrXEtjbsdDzbPEY]{Undead Influence (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.1CCRqQC3LzYkpAhs]{Vengeance Mark (2 Points)}

PurchasedTraits.Description: You have 3 ancestry points to spend on the following traits. (Quick Build: Bloodless, Undead Influence.)

FormerLife.AdvancementDescription: Choose exactly one People you were before you died. You keep that People’s size, your speed is 5, and you get no other traits from that People unless you buy Previous Life: 1 Point or Previous Life: 2 Points, which pick purchased traits from this People only. Pick your Former Life before configuring Previous Life.

PureHuman.Name: Former Life: Pure Human
PureHuman.Description:
You were a Pure Human before you died. Your size is that People’s size and your speed is 5. You don’t receive any other ancestral traits from that People unless you buy them with Previous Life: 1 Point or Previous Life: 2 Points, which can only pick purchased traits from this People.

Size: 1M. Speed: 5.

Previous Life options: 1-point: Can’t Take Hold, Perseverance, Resist the Unnatural. 2-point: Determination, Staying Power.

Corran.Name: Former Life: Corran
Corran.Description:
You were a Corran before you died. Your size is that People’s size and your speed is 5. You don’t receive any other ancestral traits from that People unless you buy them with Previous Life: 1 Point or Previous Life: 2 Points, which can only pick purchased traits from this People.

Size: 1M. Speed: 5.

Previous Life options: 1-point: Grounded, Stand Tough, Stone Shaper. 2-point: Great Fortitude, Hardened Hide.

Elvani.Name: Former Life: Elvani
Elvani.Description:
You were an Elvani before you died. Your size is that People’s size and your speed is 5. You don’t receive any other ancestral traits from that People unless you buy them with Previous Life: 1 Point or Previous Life: 2 Points, which can only pick purchased traits from this People.

Size: 1M. Speed: 5.

Previous Life options: 1-point: Graceful Retreat, High Senses, Revisit Memory. 2-point: Glamor of Terror, Otherworldly Grace, Unstoppable Mind.

Goliar.Name: Former Life: Goliar
Goliar.Description:
You were a Goliar before you died. Your size is that People’s size and your speed is 5. You don’t receive any other ancestral traits from that People unless you buy them with Previous Life: 1 Point or Previous Life: 2 Points, which can only pick purchased traits from this People.

Size: 1M. Speed: 5.

Previous Life options: 1-point: Bloodfire Rush, Grounded, Passionate Artisan. 2-point: Glowing Recovery, Nonstop.

Changer.Name: Former Life: Changer
Changer.Description:
You were a Changer before you died. Your size is that People’s size and your speed is 5. You don’t receive any other ancestral traits from that People unless you buy them with Previous Life: 1 Point or Previous Life: 2 Points, which can only pick purchased traits from this People.

Size: 1M, or 1S if you were a Rat-lineage Changer (use the Revenant (Small) ancestry for 1S). Speed: 5.

Previous Life options: 1-point: Beast’s Resolve, Layered Hide, Pack Guard. 2-point: Beast Movement, Feral Cry, Savage Burst. You don’t keep a Lineage or Changer Forms.

Mutant.Name: Former Life: Mutant
Mutant.Description:
You were a Mutant before you died. Your size is that People’s size and your speed is 5. You don’t receive any other ancestral traits from that People unless you buy them with Previous Life: 1 Point or Previous Life: 2 Points, which can only pick purchased traits from this People.

Size: 1M. Speed: 5.

Previous Life options: 1-point: Barbed Mutation, Taint Flare, Taint Sight, Warped Legs. 2-point: Membrane Wings, Ossified Crown, Prehensile Mutation.

Cyborg.Name: Former Life: Cyborg
Cyborg.Description:
You were a Cyborg before you died. Your size is that People’s size and your speed is 5. You don’t receive any other ancestral traits from that People unless you buy them with Previous Life: 1 Point or Previous Life: 2 Points, which can only pick purchased traits from this People.

Size: 1M. Speed: 5.

Previous Life options: 1-point: Auxiliary Limbs — Athletics, Penetration Optics, Predictive Sensors. 2-point: Auxiliary Limbs — Combat, Installed Suite, Locked Processors.

ToughButWithered.Name: Tough But Withered
ToughButWithered.Description:
Your undead body grants you immunity to cold, corruption, lightning, and poison damage equal to [[lookup @level]]{your level}, but you have fire weakness 5. You can’t suffocate, and you don’t need to eat or drink to stay alive.

Additionally, when your Stamina reaches the negative of your winded value, you become inert instead of dying. You fall prone and can’t stand. You continue to observe your surroundings, but you can’t speak, take main actions, maneuvers, move actions, or triggered actions. While inert this way, if you take any fire damage, your body is destroyed and you die. Otherwise, after 12 hours, you [[/heal @recoveries.recoveryValue]]{regain Stamina} equal to your recovery value.

Bloodless.Name: Bloodless
Bloodless.Description: For you, an open wound is indistinguishable from a scratch. You can’t be made bleeding even while dying.

PreviousLife1.Name: Previous Life: 1 Point
PreviousLife1.Description: Choose one purchased trait that costs 1 ancestry point from your Former Life People’s trait list. You gain that trait. You can only pick from the People you chose for Former Life. For example, a Former Life: Corran can pick Grounded, Stand Tough, or Stone Shaper.
PreviousLife1.AdvancementDescription: Pick one 1-point purchased trait from your Former Life People. Traits from other Peoples are disabled. If every option is disabled, configure Former Life first.

PreviousLife2.Name: Previous Life: 2 Points
PreviousLife2.Description: Choose one purchased trait that costs 2 ancestry points from your Former Life People’s trait list. You gain that trait. You can only pick from the People you chose for Former Life. For example, a Former Life: Corran can pick Great Fortitude or Hardened Hide.
PreviousLife2.AdvancementDescription: Pick one 2-point purchased trait from your Former Life People. Traits from other Peoples are disabled. If every option is disabled, configure Former Life first.

UndeadInfluence.Name: Undead Influence
UndeadInfluence.Description: Your supernatural gifts allow you to influence other undead. You gain an edge on Logic, Instinct, and Persona tests made to interact with undead creatures.

VengeanceMark.Name: Vengeance Mark
VengeanceMark.Description:
As a maneuver, you place a magic sigil on a creature within 10 squares. When you place a sigil, you decide where it appears on the creature’s body, and whether the sigil is visible to only you or to all creatures.

You always know the direction to the exact location of a creature who bears one of your sigils and is on the same world. You can have a number of active sigils equal to [[lookup @level]]{your level}, and can remove a sigil from a creature at will (no action required). If you already have the maximum number of sigils activated and you place a new one, your oldest sigil disappears with no other effect.

Additionally, you have the following signature ability. Signature abilities can be used at will.

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.3zJpWFMccRzRgK1y]{Detonate Sigil}

VengeanceMarkAbility.Name: Vengeance Mark
VengeanceMarkAbility.Effect:
As a maneuver, you place a magic sigil on a creature within 10 squares. When you place a sigil, you decide where it appears on the creature’s body, and whether the sigil is visible to only you or to all creatures. [[/apply h5HrY0cC4yFo2740]]

You always know the direction to the exact location of a creature who bears one of your sigils and is on the same world. You can have a number of active sigils equal to [[lookup @level]]{your level}, and can remove a sigil from a creature at will (no action required). If you already have the maximum number of sigils activated and you place a new one, your oldest sigil disappears with no other effect.
VengeanceMarkAbility.StatusDescription: You always know the direction to the exact location of a creature who bears one of your sigils and is on the same world. You can have a number of active sigils equal to your level, and can remove a sigil from a creature at will (no action required). If you already have the maximum number of sigils activated and you place a new one, your oldest sigil disappears with no other effect.

DetonateSigil.Name: Detonate Sigil
DetonateSigil.Story: A magic sigil you placed on a creature explodes with energy.

SpecSheet.Name: Spec Sheet
SpecSheet.Description: Choose one Technical skill you already have. Whenever you obtain a low result on an easy or medium test using this skill, you treat it as a middle result instead. Additionally, if you spend 1 minute inspecting a device, weapon, vehicle, or piece of chrome related to the chosen skill, you can estimate its street value in ¥ and learn of any flaws in its construction — knockoff parts, bad welds, a hidden backdoor.

MasterTech.Name: Master Tech
MasterTech.Description: Whenever you make a test as part of a crafting or research project that uses a Technical skill you already have, you can make the power roll twice and use either roll.

TapeAndPrayer.Name: Tape and Prayer
TapeAndPrayer.Description: Whenever you make a test to build, mod, or repair something and don’t have a skill that applies to the test, you gain a +1 bonus to the power roll.

JuryRig.Name: Jury-Rig
JuryRig.Description: Without needing to make a test — and even without tools — you can quickly jury-rig or patch a mundane item or piece of equipment related to a Technical skill you have. The fix lasts for 1 hour or works for one use or activation (whichever comes first, as the Director determines), then fails beyond repair. For example, with Repair you could bridge a dead lift’s power long enough for your crew to ride it up, and with Electronics you could splice a burner commlink out of scrap that works for 1 hour.

CrunchShift.Name: Crunch Shift
CrunchShift.Description: When you make a project roll using a Technical skill, you can spend a hero token to make another project roll for the same project as part of the same respite activity. You can’t use this perk more than once per respite.

MobileWorkshop.Name: Mobile Workshop
MobileWorkshop.Description: On any day when you don’t take a respite, you can spend 1 uninterrupted hour working on a crafting project using a Technical skill you have — in the back of the van, on a safehouse floor, wherever. If you do so, you gain [[/r 1d10]] project points toward that project.

PushTheMeat.Name: Push the Meat
PushTheMeat.Description: Whenever you fail a Physique test, you can lose Stamina equal to [[/damage 1d6+@level]]{1d6 + your level} to improve the outcome of the test by one result (low to middle, or middle to high). You can use this perk only once per test.

UrbanCamouflage.Name: Urban Camouflage
UrbanCamouflage.Description: Whenever you are in the Reach’s abandoned or lawless strata — the Warrens, the Sinks, dead industrial levels, collapsed transit — once you are hidden from a creature, you don’t need cover or concealment to stay hidden from them.

StreetSense.Name: Street Sense
StreetSense.Description: Whenever you are in the undercity or an unsecured stratum of the Reach (but not inside a secured arcology or enclave), you gain an edge on tests made using the Perception skill, and you can’t be surprised. Additionally, you feel it in your gut when a disaster is coming within the next 72 hours — a structural collapse, a grid blackout, a gang war boiling over — though you don’t know exactly what it will be.

BoostUp.Name: Boost Up
BoostUp.Description: As a maneuver, you grab a willing adjacent ally or object of your size or smaller, then vertical push that target up to a number of squares equal to [[lookup 2*@M evaluate=true]]{twice your Physique score} — up a fire escape, onto a rooftop, over a fence. If a creature you push falls as a result of this movement, the effective distance of the fall is reduced by a number of squares equal to [[lookup 2*@M evaluate=true]]{twice your Physique score}. When you use this perk, you can’t use it again until you earn 1 or more Victories.

IveGotYou.Name: I’ve Got You
IveGotYou.Description: Whenever a willing ally falls and would land on you or adjacent to you, you can safely catch them as a free triggered action. Neither of you takes damage from the ally’s fall.

StrayWhisperer.Name: Stray Whisperer
StrayWhisperer.Description: You can use the Survival skill to interact with nonsapient creatures who aren’t animals — autopilot drones, feral lab-grown vermin, Veil-touched beasts in the Sinks.

PutYourBackIntoIt.Name: Put Your Back Into It!
PutYourBackIntoIt.Description: During montage tests, whenever you make a test to assist a test and obtain a low result, the assisted test doesn’t take a bane. Additionally, once per montage test, you can turn an ally’s low result into a middle result.

PointRunner.Name: Point Runner
PointRunner.Description: At the start of a group test or montage test, you can spend a hero token. If you do, all participants make tests as if they also had any skill you have from the Action skill group.

CrewWork.Name: Crew Work
CrewWork.Description: When you take your first turn during any montage test, you can both make a test and assist another hero’s test.

ConcreteWise.Name: Concrete Wise
ConcreteWise.Description: When you make a test using a skill from the Action skill group and at least one of the d10s rolled is a 1, you can reroll one d10. You can use this perk only once per test.

SilverTongue.Name: Silver Tongue
SilverTongue.Description: If you fail a test using the Deception skill, you don’t suffer any consequences associated with the failure. Additionally, during a negotiation, you can be caught in one lie without negative consequences. When you use either benefit of this perk, you can’t use this perk again until you earn 1 or more Victories.

Headliner.Name: Headliner
Headliner.Description: Whenever a creature watches you sing, dance, play a set, or perform a role (as an actor, not just in disguise) for 1 uninterrupted minute or more — live or on a stream — you gain an edge on any test made to influence that creature for 1 hour after the performance ends.

Soapbox.Name: Soapbox
Soapbox.Description: Whenever you are not in combat, you can shout to get the attention of hearing creatures within 10 squares of you. Each such creature who is not hostile toward you listens to what you have to say for 1 uninterrupted minute or more, or until they sense danger or any form of imminent harm. While creatures are listening to you, each of your allies gains an edge on tests made to avoid being noticed by those creatures.

FrequencyMatch.Name: Frequency Match
FrequencyMatch.Description: You can make a Persona test using the Performance skill to influence creatures who don’t have emotions or can’t understand you — a security AI, a guard drone, a burned-out augment. Additionally, once during a negotiation when an ally makes an argument, you can drop the right track or the right rhythm to give that ally an edge on their test.

BullshitDetector.Name: Bullshit Detector
BullshitDetector.Description: In response to another creature communicating information to you, you can spend a hero token to determine whether that information contained any knowing lies. If so, you know what the lies are, but not what the truth is.

OffTheRecord.Name: Off the Record
OffTheRecord.Description: Whenever you speak one-on-one with a creature, you can ask them one question about themself that might typically offend them or raise suspicion. If they choose not to answer honestly, they simply deflect or redirect the question, with no further complications. If they choose to answer honestly, the creature can immediately ask you a question about yourself in turn, which you must answer honestly.

PardonMyFriend.Name: Pardon My Friend
PardonMyFriend.Description: When an ally within 5 squares fails a Persona test, you can step in and make a Persona test that takes a bane, with your roll replacing the ally’s roll. This perk can be used only once per test, even if more than one character has it.

MuscleTalks.Name: Muscle Talks
MuscleTalks.Description: Whenever you make a test that uses the Performance, Persuasion, or Intimidation skill to posture, flirt, or threaten, you can use Physique instead of any other characteristic the test calls for.

SoTellMe.Name: So Tell Me …
SoTellMe.Description: Whenever you succeed on a Persona test to influence one or more creatures, you can ask one creature you influenced a follow-up question after the test resolves, which they must answer honestly. At the Director’s discretion, the creature doesn’t have to answer the question completely — or at all — if the response would put them or someone they love in danger.

SpotTheTell.Name: Spot the Tell
SpotTheTell.Description: Whenever you make a test to read a person and obtain a high result, you notice several tells that give away their true feelings — a pupil flutter, a micro-twitch in a cyber-jaw, a heartbeat spike. Any test you make to read that person in the future gains an edge.

ShadowNetwork.Name: Shadow Network
ShadowNetwork.Description: You have a network of fixers, fences, and street contacts. As a respite activity while you take a respite in a district or enclave, you can ask your contacts a question by making a Persona test. On a middle result, you learn one piece of information that would be common on the street — the back ways into a building, where a wanted runner is holed up, the name of the local gang boss, and so forth. On a high result, you can instead learn something uncommon on the street, as long as such information exists — the location of a hidden stash, the gun used in an executive’s assassination, the fixer secretly bankrolling a local hit crew, and so forth.

ForgettableFace.Name: Forgettable Face
ForgettableFace.Description:
If you spend 10 minutes or less interacting with a creature who hasn’t met you before, you can cause them to forget your face when you part. If asked to describe you, the creature gives only a vague, blank, and unhelpful description — and street cams somehow never get a clean frame.

Additionally, if you spend 1 hour or more assembling a disguise, you automatically obtain a middle result on any test to pass as someone else. If you have the Deception skill, you automatically obtain a high result on the test.

GumUpTheWorks.Name: Gum Up the Works
GumUpTheWorks.Description: Whenever a mundane trap or security countermeasure activates within 3 squares — a tripwire, a pressure plate, a sentry-turret trigger — you can use a triggered action to move up to 3 squares toward it. If this movement brings you adjacent to any of its mechanisms, you can jam it, preventing it from activating. As long as you stay adjacent to the mechanism, it can’t go off unless an attempt to disarm it fails.

LuckyDog.Name: Lucky Dog
LuckyDog.Description: Whenever you fail a test using an intrigue skill (Stealth, Deception, Security Systems, Perception, or Demolitions), you can lose Stamina equal to [[/damage 1d6+@level]]{1d6 + your level} to improve the outcome of the test by one result. You can use this perk only once per test.

QuickChange.Name: Quick Change
QuickChange.Description: You can don or remove a disguise as part of any test you make using the Stealth skill, or while using the Hide maneuver.

SlippedCuffs.Name: Slipped Cuffs
SlippedCuffs.Description: You gain an edge on tests made to escape restraints. Given 1 uninterrupted minute, you can escape any mundane restraints — zip-cuffs, mag-cuffs, duct tape — without making a test. Additionally, it’s not immediately obvious when you’ve escaped restraints until you do something that makes it clear you have done so (cast them off, use an ability that harms one or more creatures, and so forth).

ButIKnowWhoDoes.Name: But I Know Who Does
ButIKnowWhoDoes.Description: Whenever you fail a test to recall lore using a skill from the Knowledge skill group, you instinctively recall the nearest place where the information you seek might be found — a data broker’s den, a corp archive, a sealed Wired node, a Veil-reader in the Sinks, or any other location of the Director’s determination. The Director can decide that certain lore can’t be revealed this way.

EideticMemory.Name: Eidetic Memory
EideticMemory.Description: Your mind is a data vault, though not always a well-indexed one. When you finish a respite, choose one skill from the Knowledge skill group that you don’t have. You have that skill until you finish your next respite. Additionally, if you spend 1 uninterrupted minute or more reading any page of text or screen of data, you can memorize its contents, allowing you to memorize entire manuals with sufficient time.

DataMiner.Name: Data Miner
DataMiner.Description: Whenever you make a test as part of a crafting or research project using a skill from the Knowledge skill group, you can make the power roll twice and use either roll.

IveSeenTheFeeds.Name: I’ve Seen the Feeds
IveSeenTheFeeds.Description:
Each time you enter a district, arcology, or enclave you’ve never been to before, you can ask the Director one of the following questions:

  • Who is the most influential public figure here?

  • Who here would be the friendliest to us right now?

  • What does this place need most from outsiders?

If the Director doesn’t have an answer to the question you ask, or doesn’t want to answer, you can instead ask a different question.

Polyglot.Name: Polyglot
Polyglot.Description: You automatically learn two new languages, as long as you have regularly heard those languages spoken or seen them written before. Additionally, if you spend 7 days or more in a place where you regularly hear or read a language you don’t know — a street market, a corp satellite office, an enclave — you can pick up enough of it to hold a conversation or understand basic written information. Having picked up a language this way, you can subsequently learn it using the Learn New Language research project at half the usual project goal cost.

WikiBrain.Name: Wiki Brain
WikiBrain.Description: Whenever you make a test to recall lore and don’t have a skill that applies to the test, you gain a +1 bonus to the power roll.

Specialist.Name: Specialist
Specialist.Description: You are a leading expert on a particular subject. Choose one skill you have from the Knowledge skill group. You always have a double edge on tests made to recall lore using this skill. Additionally, your expertise gives you a name in related circles. You treat your Renown as 1 higher when negotiating with an NPC who knows your reputation, or 2 higher if they have the same skill you chose for this perk.

RemoteResearch.Name: Remote Research
RemoteResearch.Description: On any day when you don’t take a respite, you can spend 1 uninterrupted hour working on a research project using a skill you have from the Knowledge skill group — on a slate, in a data café, on a transit ride. If you do so, you gain [[/r 1d10]] project points toward that project.

VeilTrick.Name: Veil Trick
VeilTrick.Description: You pull a small, showy working through the Veil.

SignalRead.Name: Signal Read
SignalRead.Description: As a maneuver, choose a creature within 10 squares and read its Signal. If that creature is your level or lower, you learn the keywords in their stat block (Humanoid, Construct, Undead, and so forth).

VeilFamiliar.Name: Veil Familiar
VeilFamiliar.Description:
A small Veil-spirit has taken up residence in a specific small animal or scrap object — an alley rat, a rooftop pigeon, a broken toy drone — and chosen to be your familiar, or adopted you as theirs.

The spirit uses the @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel.monsters.Actor.cBkB3TyhBE1UsNGM]{familiar} stat block.

The familiar can hold small objects in their mouth, claws, or grabber, but can’t perform activities that would typically require hands (opening a door, working a keypad, and so forth). They can’t harm other creatures or objects. They can flank in combat, but only with you.

If your familiar is destroyed, you can restore them as a respite activity, or by spending a Recovery as a main action to call them back into an unoccupied space adjacent to you.

GhostTouch.Name: Ghost Touch
GhostTouch.Description: You nudge a tiny object through the Signal.

WireWhisper.Name: Wire Whisper
WireWhisper.Description: You send a one-way message through the Signal straight into a friend’s head.

StreetBlessing.Name: Street Blessing
StreetBlessing.Description: You can spend 1 uninterrupted minute to perform a Veil ritual of blessing — chalk sigils, a lit candle, a whispered name — targeting yourself or one willing creature you touch. The target has a double edge on the next test they make within the next minute. A target can’t use this benefit on an activity that takes longer than 1 minute.

EchoReader.Name: Echo Reader
EchoReader.Description:
When you hold an object in your hand for 1 uninterrupted minute, you can sense whether it carries an emotional echo in the Signal. Objects with an echo could include treasured gifts, murder weapons, or personal keepsakes. If the Director determines that the object carries an echo, you learn the most dominant emotion attached to it, then receive a flash that answers one of the following questions:

  • What was the name of the person whose emotion is imprinted on this object?

  • Why does this emotion linger on the object?

  • How long has it been since the object was held by the person whose emotion lingers on it?

After asking one question, you can choose to dig deeper by asking one additional question from the list, but you are then overcome with emotions that aren’t yours. You take a bane on Instinct and Persona tests until you finish a respite, and you can’t use this perk again while you suffer this bane.

VeilTrick.Name: Veil Trick
VeilTrick.Story: You pull a small, showy working through the Veil — the kind of street magic that buys a round of drinks.
VeilTrick.Effect_before0000000000:
Choose one of the following effects:

  • You blink a size 1S or smaller object adjacent to you into an unoccupied space adjacent to you.

  • Until the start of your next turn, a part of your body throws a shower of harmless, crackling Veil-sparks that light up each square adjacent to you.

  • You kill or wake (your choice) every mundane light source of size 1L or smaller adjacent to you — a streetlamp, a neon tube, a lighter.

  • You make up to 1 pound of food you touch taste delicious or disgusting. Vat-protein counts.

  • Until the start of your next turn, your body gives off a particular smell you’ve smelled before. Each creature within 5 squares of you can sense it, but it can’t impose any condition or other drawback on them.

  • You leave a small glowing Veil-tag on the surface of a mundane object you touch, or you erase a tag made by you or by another creature using Veil Trick.

  • You touch a size 1T object and glamour it to look like a different object. Any creature who handles the object becomes aware of the glamour. It ends when you stop touching the object.

GhostTouch.Name: Ghost Touch
GhostTouch.Story: A Signal flex — you nudge something small without laying a hand on it.
GhostTouch.Effect_before0000000000: You can grab or manipulate the target object through the Signal, moving it up to a number of squares equal to [[lookup formula="max(@R, @I, @P)" evaluate=true]]{your Logic, Instinct, or Persona score (your choice)}. You can use this ability to turn a handle, flip a breaker, tap a keypad, and so forth. You can manipulate any small movable piece of a larger object as long as the piece is unattended and size 1T. You can’t use this ability to break a smaller piece off a larger object.

WireWhisper.Name: Wire Whisper
WireWhisper.Story: You drop a one-way message straight into a friend’s head — no commlink, no trace on the Wired.
WireWhisper.Effect_before0000000000: As long as the target understands one or more languages, you send them a message through the Signal that takes 10 seconds or less to speak. It arrives like a voice on a private channel. The target knows who the message is from and can decide to ignore it and subsequent messages.

Warnings.StockPerk: {name} is a Draw Steel perk. Ghostwire uses the Ghostwire Perks compendium — pick a perk from there.

Wired.Label: Wired
Wired.Hint: Your connection to the Wired. Connect enters Overlay; Toggle Connection State switches Overlay and Jacked In; Jack Out disconnects.

StateHints.overlay: Overlay: bane on real-world ability power rolls.
StateHints.jackedIn: Jacked In: edge on Wired power rolls; body inert, no real-world power rolls.

Warnings.NotConnected: {actor} isn’t connected to the Wired. Use Connect first.
Warnings.AlreadyConnected: {actor} is already connected to the Wired ({state}). Use Toggle Connection State or Jack Out.
Warnings.JackedInPhysical: {actor} is Jacked In: their body is inert and can’t use {name}. Toggle to Overlay or Jack Out first.

Wired.Migrated: Ghostwire: added Matrix Verbs to {count} existing hero(es).
